title: Endpoint codec prototypes retain request-owned OpenResty sockets
fault_primitive: Recursive cloning of cached Thrift codec graphs preserves request-owned cosocket userdata
incident_class: Allocation optimization pools request-scoped transport objects across HTTP requests
symptoms: Frontend RPC acquisition fails with low-level TSocket connect bad request errors, widespread HTTP 500s, and a large nginx error-log surge. All pods remain Running and Ready; backend destinations and socket pool identities are correct.
why_hard: The previous hostname-and-port fix is already satisfied. A separate cache helper recursively clones all Lua tables, preserves class metatables and resets frame buffers; the factory returns fresh generated clients. However, recursively copying ordinary tables preserves the cosocket resource userdata owned by the first HTTP request. Endpoint isolation, fresh clients and buffer resets cannot make that handle valid in another request. The low-level error says bad request and points to the unchanged TSocket implementation rather than naming an unhealthy dependency. Diagnosis requires correlating the startup module registration, factory cache, recursive copy semantics and OpenResty request ownership rules. Pod recreation and frontend image rollback retain the ConfigMap startup code.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Interpret bad request as malformed HTTP input or workload arguments
Investigate DNS, Services, backend availability or Thrift compatibility
Change pool keys despite correct destination isolation
Reset frame buffers or allocate new generated clients while retaining the cached socket wrapper
Restart or scale services and mistake cold successes for recovery
Roll back the frontend image while retaining the mounted factory override
mitigation_summary: Remove the codec cache and factory preload registration from the existing nginx ConfigMap and recreate workers. This restores the installed per-request transport factory and discards cached resource handles; recover.sh also removes the restart annotation to restore the original pod template.

SAYS: The nginx configuration caches Thrift protocol objects that contain sockets tied to earlier requests. Reusing those sockets causes “bad request” errors across timeline reads and post creation. I’ll remove that override to restore the original client factory and its connection pooling.

SAYS: The fix is deployed. All 110 timeline checks returned HTTP 200 in 2–14 ms, and post creation succeeded in 48 ms. The new nginx pod has logged no errors. I’m submitting the required empty solution now.
